title: FLMOP 25, 2026
author: Adam Boxer
summary: Adam Boxer presents FLMOP, Front Loading the Means of Participation, as one of the simplest and most effective behaviour management strategies available to teachers. He opens with a written scenario of a science lesson in which loose, conversational instructions let a gentle background hubbub build, then contrasts it with video of the same teacher's calm, focused class. Drawing on Doug Lemov's idea of the means of participation, he argues that teachers must state how students should act, such as in complete silence, because students will not intuit it. His key move is about sequence: if the instruction comes first, students are already acting on it and never hear the behavioural expectation, so the means of participation must come before the instruction. Boxer closes with provisos, noting that FLMOP is a nudge rather than a guarantee, that reminders mid-instruction help, and that it combines well with other strategies such as anticipating triggers.
points: Loose, conversational instructions communicate loose behavioural norms, and low-level hubbub early in a lesson can escalate into real disruption.
Teachers must explicitly state the means of participation, such as silently or on a mini-whiteboard, because students will not infer it.
Order matters: once students hear an instruction they start acting on it, so an expectation placed after the instruction goes unheard.
FLMOP is a behavioural nudge rather than a guarantee, and it works best alongside strategies like anticipating triggers with a 'when I say go' cue.
quotes: I also worry that while it might seem innocuous now, by the end of the lesson the hubbub has escalated into more substantial disruption. This happens because the behavioural norms that Tom is communicating are loose and conversational.

When I first started really learning how to manage behaviour, FLMOP was one of the first strategies I used, and in those early days made a huge difference to the overall calmness and productivity of my lessons.
If we want students to act in a certain way, we need to tell them what that is.
This script is definitely better than the original scenario, because if specifies the means of participation, and a good rule is that if we don’t specify it, students won’t intuit it by themselves.
Unfortunately, if the students heard the instruction, then they are already acting on it, and are unlikely to hear and properly assimilate the means of participation.
This is called Front Loading the Means of Participation, or FLMOP for short, and it’s an extremely powerful way to create a classroom culture which is calm, quiet and efficient.
FLMOP is a kind of behavioural nudge that gets students closer to doing the thing you want them to. Any teacher can do it, and in the majority of cases it will make a significant difference.
